transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. I guess... well, I'm a nurse, and I really love my job, I always try to do my very best. But the main reason I made the appointment is that when I'm on the floor, I just... I kind of lose my train of thought constantly? 

Like, I know hospitals are naturally noisy and I should be used to it, but if an IV pump beeps, or even if I just hear someone ask another nurse a question, or a call light goes off down the hall... suddenly I've completely forgotten what patient flow issue I was just working on. I feel awful even admitting that because I don't want to sound incompetent, I promise I work really hard. It's just getting a bit frustrating. Is... is that something you see a lot? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
How long have you been experiencing these difficulties with losing your train of thought?

Well, um... I guess I've always been a little easily sidetracked, maybe? But it really became a... well, a major problem almost two years ago. That's when I took on these expanded charge-nurse responsibilities. 

I was so incredibly grateful they trusted me with the role, I really was! But with all the extra moving parts and people needing me, it just got a lot harder to hide the fact that I was losing my place all the time. I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I can't handle the work—I promise I always make sure the patients are perfectly safe and everything gets done. It's just... I have to work so much harder to keep my thoughts straight now. Does that make sense? Is it normal for things to get worse when your duties change like that?
Looking back to your childhood or school years, did you have similar difficulties with staying focused, being easily distracted, or keeping organized?

Um, well... I guess, if I really think back... yes? Maybe a little bit? I mean, I always got decent grades, I promise I was a good student! But... um... my mom did have to help me quite a bit. She would sit with me every single night just to make sure I was actually doing my homework and not just staring at the wall. 

And, um... I feel so silly saying this, but my teachers in elementary school, they were always really sweet, but they used to write on my report cards that I was... well, they said I was bright, which was nice! But they also said I was a bit careless. I would do the worksheets and then just... lose them? Or forget to hand them in. I know that sounds terrible, like I just didn't care, but I really did! I just couldn't seem to keep track of my papers. Is that... is that the kind of thing you mean? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it was.
Aside from work, do you find yourself constantly worrying about a variety of everyday things, even when there is no clear reason to?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I care about things, of course! I want everything to go well, especially for my family and my patients. But I wouldn't say I'm constantly worrying about everything. 

I try to stay really positive, you know? Sometimes I might stress a little bit if I'm running late or if I misplace my keys again—which happens more than I'd like to admit, I'm so sorry to say—but I don't just sit around worrying for no reason. I hope that's a good thing? I really try not to be a burden or a worrywart. Is it okay that I don't feel that way?
